subject: general
question: The Prarthana Samaj, which was recognised as an institution that worked for religious as well as social reform, was established in Bombay by _______ in 1867.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Dr Atma Ram Pandurang**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Prarthana Samaj movement also referred to as the "Prayer Society,**" was a religious and social reform **movement in Bombay,** India, modelled after earlier reform movements.
 
• When **Keshub Chandra Sen** visited Maharashtra in 1863, **Dadoba Pandurang **and his brother **Atmaram Pandurang established the Prarthana Samaj.** It was done with the intention of converting people to monotheistic belief and worship. When **Mahadev Govind Ranade** joined, it became more well-known.
 
• The intellectuals who favoured changes to the Hindu social order were the key reformers. Its dissemination in southern India was aided by Telugu reformer and writer **Kandukuri Veeresalingam.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Prarthana Samaj**

 
 
• **​**​The movement was started by **Atmaram Panduranga,** and after reformer and **scholar Mahadev Govind Ranade** joined it, it acquired speed and popularity.
 
• The Samaj was distinct from the **Bengali Brahmo Samaj** in that it was less extreme and approached reformist programmes with caution. It also garnered better feedback from the general population as a result.
 
• The group's members all identified as Hindus and did so throughout. They want internal religious reform. They weren't opposed to religion per se; rather, they were against the societal ills that were common at the time, such as child marriage, widow repression, dowry, sati, untouchability, etc.
 
• They also promoted **monotheism and condemned** the worship of idols.
 
• Meetings of the society were held behind closed doors out of concern for a reaction from the orthodoxy. In actuality, neither the orthodox segments of society nor Brahminical power was ever specifically assailed by the Prarthana Samaj.
 
• The **Brahmo Samaj and the Arya Samaj of Dayananda Saraswati** had a significant impact on the Samaj, although it persisted as a separate organisation.
 
• Along with Ranade, the **Sanskrit scholar Sir Ramakrishna Gopal Bhandarkar **and the political figure **Sir Narayan Chandavarkar** were significant Samaj members.
